statement: Every inbound artifact (browser upload, API upload, every API record batch, scheduled pull, SFTP pull, partner webhook-triggered fetch, mailroom vendor delivery) MUST enter through one ingestion boundary that records an Artifact (custody: slot, quarantine, inspection, storage, retention). Command batches, observation sets and reference datasets are then processed by a Run under a named profile; evidence documents attach to their case directly after release, without a Run. No delivery adapter MAY parse business content, apply business rules or write domain tables.
rationale: Prevents each channel from growing its own rules (mission §9); one place to secure, audit and test.
source: unbound#18 ('portal/API and future managed file-transfer adapters under same policy'); mission §9
responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component (component monolith) on Echelon.Execution
acceptance: Given a grant-recommendation CSV delivered once by browser upload and once by API upload with identical bytes, When both are processed, Then both produce the same Run outcomes, the same validation messages and the same command payloads, and the second is detected as a duplicate artifact.
verification: Integration test + Architectural review (static rule: adapters reference only the boundary API)
discovery_source: unbound#18; echelon-organization-administration#20; file-ingestion and STP mission (2026-11-26)

statement: Records from command-batch artifacts MUST become the same Echelon.Execution operations, at the same contract version, that interactive clients submit, and MUST pass the same server-side authorization, validation, policy and approval at execution; the preview MUST call each command handler's side-effect-free validate mode rather than re-implementing business rules in profile catalogs; an ingestion profile MUST NOT name an operation that has no interactive equivalent, and no ingestion code MAY write to ledger, fact or reservation tables.
rationale: A file must never be a privileged path around controls (mission §9, §14).
source: unbound#18 ('no direct financial writes'); mission §14; CNV-PLT-010
responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component (component monolith) on Echelon.Execution
acceptance: Given a donor whose grant authority was revoked after uploading a bulk file, When the Run submits, Then every row's grant.recommend command is Declined at execution with the same reason an interactive request would receive, and no ledger row exists for any of them.
verification: Integration test + static analysis (no ingestion module references ledger write APIs)
discovery_source: unbound#18; echelon-organization-administration#20; file-ingestion and STP mission (2026-11-26)

statement: Every ingestion profile MUST declare exactly one artifact class (command-batch, observation-set, reference-dataset, evidence-document, configuration) and the output kind it produces; observation-sets MUST be recorded append-only as external observations (UNB-XIN-EVA-016) and MUST NOT create or move money; reference-datasets MUST be activated as whole snapshots; evidence-documents MUST attach to an owning case or command and yield extraction proposals only.

statement: Inspection and parsing MUST enforce per-profile and platform limits on bytes, records, fields per record, field length, pages, pixels, frames, nesting depth, archive entries, total expansion and per-entry expansion ratio, CPU time, memory and wall time, counting while streaming rather than trusting declared sizes; exceeding any limit MUST reject the artifact with the limit named.

statement: Parsing, normalisation, image decoding and PDF rasterisation MUST run in a sandbox created per artifact with no network, no database access and no cloud credentials: a trusted supervisor (an Echelon.Execution worker) claims the command, fetches the object with a credential scoped to that tenant and that single object version, verifies the hash, passes the bytes to the sandbox and receives typed records and derivatives back; the supervisor validates the output against the record schema, recomputes control totals in managed code that does not parse the file, and writes staging rows under the tenant's own database role with row-level security. The sandbox is a second deployment unit of the same codebase (not a new codebase), and its isolation primitive is an owner decision (FIL-OD-13).
rationale: Parser vulnerabilities (FIE-C-033..035) must not reach application secrets or the network; a role, not a new service.
source: unbound#18 ('isolated least-privilege parser/scanner with no arbitrary network access'); mission §12
responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component, inspector role (isolated deployment of the same binary)
acceptance: Given a sandbox fixture that attempts an outbound connection, reads environment variables and emits an extra record with matching totals, When the artifact is processed, Then the connection fails, no credential is present in the sandbox, the supervisor's independently computed totals disagree and the Run is Held with SEC-SANDBOX-OUTPUT-MISMATCH.

statement: Every artifact's exact immutable bytes MUST be inspected by a managed or licensed malware engine before release (the cloud provider's on-upload object scanning where available, otherwise a licensed engine deployed inside the platform network); the inspection command MUST obtain the verdict by polling the scan result bound to the object version id and the recorded SHA-256 through its existing storage access (event routing is optional and only reduces latency, so no broker is introduced); multi-tenant public scanning services that share submitted content MUST NOT be used; no custom antivirus engine MAY be built.

statement: Uploads MUST follow slot-first ordering: (1) commit an Artifact row in Receiving with expected size limits; (2) accept bytes through short-lived write-only, resumable multipart upload bound to the generated key and size range with per-part checksums (or stream server-side for pulls); (3) verify the whole-artifact SHA-256 on the server and, on storage confirmation, commit Quarantined with hash and enqueue inspection in the same transaction. A reconciler MUST abandon expired slots and delete their partial objects, and MUST report objects without rows and rows without objects.
rationale: Interrupted operations, orphans and missing objects reconcile deterministically (mission §13).
responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component + managed object storage (cloud-provided)
acceptance: Given a browser upload that stops at 60% and never resumes, When the slot lifetime passes, Then the Artifact is Abandoned, the partial object is deleted, and the reconciler's daily report shows zero orphans.

statement: Two storage containers per environment MUST be used: a quarantine container (scanner attached, no application read except the supervisor, objects expire after the quarantine retention period) and a records container (versioned, encrypted with provider-managed keys per environment, legal hold enabled). Write-once retention MUST be applied only after a short correction window (proposed 7 days) during which a misfiled upload can be deleted under dual control with a tombstone; storage-enforced retention MUST use a mode that permits court- or regulator-ordered and privacy-mandated deletion under dual control (not a mode that even administrators cannot lift). An object MUST be copied to records only after a committed clean verdict.
rationale: Unscanned bytes are never readable by the application; retention and legal hold are enforced by storage, not only by code.
responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component + managed object storage (cloud-provided)
acceptance: Given an artifact released at 10:00, When the records copy completes, Then the records object carries a retention date derived from its retention class and the quarantine object is deleted at its expiry.
discovery_source: unbound#18; echelon-organization-administration#20; file-ingestion and STP mission (2026-11-26)

responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component + managed object storage (cloud-provided)

statement: No record MAY be silently discarded: every input record MUST reach a visible outcome (Invalid with field, position and reason; Duplicate with the original; Excluded with actor and reason; Declined; Effected; or OutcomeUnknown), and the sum of outcome counts MUST equal the input record count, checked automatically for every Run.

statement: Duplicate detection MUST operate at three levels and distinguish duplicates from conflicts (UNB-XIN-EVA-005): artifact (tenant-, purpose- and source-scoped SHA-256 and source file id; the same business date and sequence with a different hash is a conflict case that holds both runs); record (profile-declared natural key plus a canonical payload hash: same key and same hash is Duplicate and has no effect; same key and different hash is KeyConflict, not applied, with a DuplicateKeyConflict case; a key collision within one artifact makes the record Invalid; where a source omits its reference the key falls back to file id and record sequence); and near-duplicate (declared fields without a shared key, held for a decision, never dropped).

responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component + target domain command handlers

responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component + target domain command handlers

statement: Controlled replay MUST create a new Run from a Released artifact under a stated profile version with actor, reason and authority. statement: Document content MUST be treated as untrusted data: extraction calls MUST receive one document (or page set) and a fixed task, MUST have no tools, no retrieval and no access to other records, and MUST return output only through a strict schema. Extraction MUST run on the same rasterised derivative shown to the reviewer; where a text layer is also used, any raster/text disagreement on an extracted field sets the injection flag and blocks one-click confirmation. The injection flag MUST come from deterministic detectors (instruction patterns, hidden or off-page text, raster/text disagreement) as well as model output and is never the only control.
rationale: Prompt injection through documents (FIE-C-049, FIE-C-050).

acceptance: Given a custodian adds a column to its position file, When the next file arrives under a profile with unknown_fields refuse-run, Then the Run is Held with ONB-SCHEMA-DRIFT naming the new column, and yesterday's data remain in effect.

statement: Every expected non-ACH contribution (wire, check, securities, DAF-to-DAF, intermediary proceeds) MUST be declared as a contribution intent that issues a unique reference and the sponsor's receiving instructions containing it (wire memo, DTC note or FFC line, check memo, remittance coupon); matching MUST use that reference first, and unidentified receipts MUST enter suspense with ageing.
rationale: Industry intake is pooled receipt plus free-text attribution; the reference prevents most orphans (FIE-A-131, FIE-A-106, FIE-A-123).
source: FIE-A-131; FIE-A-106; FIE-A-123; FIE-A-135; RR-UNB-GAP-013-r1; UNB-XIN-PAY-007
responsible_system: Unbound domain components (contributions, grants, charity knowledge, migration)
acceptance: Given a donor who declared a 100-share gift of XYZ from a named delivering broker and received reference C-7Q4K, When the custodian report shows 100 XYZ from that broker with note 'C-7Q4K', Then the receipt matches automatically with rule REF-AMOUNT-SENDER-EXACT; if the delivering broker differs, it stays in Unidentified suspense with the intent as a suggestion.

rationale: Checks are an R1 instrument with no ingestion requirement (reconciliation topic 15).
responsible_system: Unbound domain components (contributions, grants, charity knowledge, migration)
acceptance: Given a lockbox batch of 37 items totalling $48,210.00 and a bank credit of $48,210.00, When processed, Then 35 items match intents, 2 open orphan cases with their images, and the batch reconciles to the credit.
open_questions: Which bank provides the launch lockbox and its layout (contract-only).

statement: For complex assets handled by the intermediary (CNV-GRT-013), Unbound MUST ingest the intermediary's acceptance, sale confirmation and proceeds as observations matched to the contribution intent, and MUST store the donor's appraisal and Form 8283 as evidence for the donee-acknowledgment signature event, applying thresholds by asset class: publicly traded securities need no appraisal and no Section B donee signature; Section B applies above $5,000; non-publicly traded stock needs a qualified appraisal only above $10,000; cryptocurrency above $5,000 needs a qualified appraisal; Form 8282 duties apply to Section B property disposed of within 3 years except items of $500 or less. Unbound MUST NOT ingest asset valuations as holdings.
rationale: Aligns document intake with the intermediary decision.

statement: Ingestion commands MUST respect the durable-queue fairness rules of unbound#15: per-tenant quotas on concurrent ingestion runs and on bytes in inspection, a lower priority class for bulk ingestion than for interactive commands, lease renewal for long-running parsing tasks, and poison isolation per artifact so one tenant's large or malformed file cannot delay another tenant's interactive work.
rationale: Queue fairness and long leases were missing (review R2-04).

acceptance: Given tenant A uploads ten 200 MB migration files while tenant B submits an interactive grant, When the queue is busy, Then B's command is claimed within its normal latency target and A's runs proceed within A's quota.

statement: Ingestion submitted by a service identity (API client, partner platform) MUST act on behalf of a named principal with recorded delegated authority for every target command; a service identity has no authority of its own to recommend grants or change funds. rationale: Machine-submitted grant batches had no authority model (review R2-06).
responsible_system: Unbound ingestion component (component monolith) on Echelon.Execution
acceptance: Given a partner API client without an on-behalf-of principal, When it submits a bulk grant artifact, Then the boundary refuses it; with a principal whose authority is revoked before execution, every command is Declined.

statement: All-or-nothing command batches (migration waves, opening balances, manual journal batches) MUST execute atomically: as one command whose handler applies every record in one transaction, or as staged effects activated by one atomic command; a record declined at execution MUST roll back the whole batch. rationale: All-or-nothing held only at validation (review R2-03).

acceptance: Given an opening-balance wave of 12,000 funds where fund 11,998 is declined at execution because its pool was closed, When the batch command runs, Then no opening entry exists for any fund and the wave returns to Validated with the failure listed.
